versions.changelog:
ai-task-hub 3.3.14

- Added "Delivery Mode Guidance" and default product path instructions—clarifies recommended flows for each capability type (result-first vs async/poll/presentation).
- Updated default host and product usage guidance: result-first and connector-first flows are now emphasized, with async/presentation as compatibility or asset-delivery follow-ups only.
- SKILL.md reorganized for clarity; section on non-recommended patterns and explicit minimal architecture rules added.
- Capability inventory and capability exposure language updated for precision.
- No new user-facing features, but significantly revised documentation and operational guidance.

- Updated audio capabilities: replaced `tts_low_cost` with `tts_report`.
- Documentation updated in SKILL.md and SKILL.zh-CN.md to reflect the new audio capability.
- Capability references in `capabilities.json` and `openapi.json` adjusted for the new `tts_report` support.
- No changes to API surface or general usage flows.

- Removed the `tts_report` audio capability from the published skill capability inventory and documentation.
- Updated version to 3.3.11.
- Synced documentation and references to reflect enabled capabilities only.

- Updated to version 3.3.10.
- Removed environment variable hints for PUBLIC_BRIDGE_ENTRY_HOST and AI_TASK_HUB_ENTRY_HOST from the requirements section in the skill metadata.
- No changes to public capability inventory or core functionality.

ai-task-hub 3.3.9

- Added support for optional environment variables `PUBLIC_BRIDGE_ENTRY_HOST` and `AI_TASK_HUB_ENTRY_HOST` in the SKILL descriptor for host-side entry host configuration.
- No changes to user-facing features or capability inventory.

- Added "Official Host Integration" section clarifying built-in host requirements and future integration guidance.
- Updated connector/runtime surface documentation for improved clarity.
- No changes to capabilities or public endpoints.
- Minor documentation improvements and typo corrections.

ai-task-hub 3.2.27

- Clarified attachment handling in documentation to favor explicit attachment bytes for execution.

- Minor adjustments to improve documentation clarity and policy accuracy.
- No code-level functional changes; documentation and reference updates only.

- Tightened attachment handling policy: the skill now only processes explicit attachment objects or bytes supplied by the host runtime, and limits uploads/URL handoff to those explicit materials.
- Updated user response policy to clarify that execution only proceeds immediately when an explicit attachment is present; implicit or background upload handling is no longer triggered.
- Documentation and wording changes to reinforce stricter boundary between host and skill, scoping all media transfers to clearly supplied attachments only.
- Version bump to 3.2.25.

ai-task-hub v3.2.24

ai-task-hub v3.2.23

- Added public upload support with new logic to auto-upload attachments through the bridge when file bytes or explicit attachment paths are detected.
- Updated internal scripts, including addition of scripts/public-upload.mjs, to handle attachment normalization and upload flow.
- Adjusted SKILL.md and Chinese documentation to clarify and document the new attachment auto-upload behavior.
- Expanded and clarified public package boundary and runtime orchestration instructions regarding attachment and upload handling.

- Adds a new user-facing response policy: user uploads (images, audio, docs, video) are processed immediately and users receive only necessary responses, with internal upload details hidden unless debugging is explicitly requested.
- Clarifies that users should not be asked for manual URLs or technical field names; attachment handling and orchestration are silent unless intervention is required.
- Updates documentation to make response expectations and user experience clearer.
- No changes to functional endpoints or contracts; all existing runtime and API behaviors are preserved.

- Added section detailing install mechanism and runtime requirements, clarifying that the skill uses bundled scripts and local binaries only.
- Stated that remote installer flows and download-to-exec chains are not used.
- No changes to capability or API behavior.

- Improved documentation for visual capability boundary: the skill now clarifies that only currently enabled public visual services are discoverable, omitting disabled or internal features from discovery and capability manifests.
- Expanded description of valid use cases and documented stricter output boundary for detection/segmentation features.
- Updated authentication documentation to clarify handling of authorization URLs and entry user key reuse during the authorization process.
- Minor editorial refinements and corrections in English and Chinese documentation.

ai-task-hub 3.2.18

- Updated skill architecture and documentation to prefer third-party agent entry via `POST /agent/public-bridge/invoke`.
- Removed direct token-based authentication in favor of bridge-based flows; no longer accepts or requires `AGENT_TASK_TOKEN`.
- Expanded metadata with explicit entrypoints for agent integration and trust.
- Clarified host/runtime responsibilities for credential handling and user authorization flows.
- Improved integration instructions and examples for OpenClaw/Codex/Claude-style agent runtimes.

ai-task-hub 3.2.17

- Updated host-side bridge endpoint guidance: third-party agent entries should use /agent/public-bridge/invoke; trusted hosts may continue with /agent/skill/bridge/invoke.
- Documented that /agent/public-bridge/invoke returns an authorization URL and entry_user_key for first-time user binding.
- Clarified that write-capable actions via public bridge require explicit user confirmation (options.confirm_write=true).
- Added instructions for headless/bot-mode follow-up actions via /user/headless-tokens and /agent/headless-task-token/issue.
- Refined host integration best practices and updated examples to reflect improved bridge flows.

- Improved external user binding logic for public bridge integration in the authentication workflow.
- Updated documentation to clarify how the public bridge handles stable external user bindings and account continuity.
- No user-facing functionality changes; requirements and API endpoints remain the same.

## ai-task-hub 3.2.6 Changelog

- Added host bridge entrypoint (`scripts/ai-task-hub-host-runner.mjs`) as the recommended agent invocation method for host-integrated flows.
- Updated documentation to clarify that direct `scripts/skill.mjs` invocation is fallback-only and should not be used by end users in typical integrations.
- Improved agent invocation quickstart instructions to reflect best practices for host runtime integration.

ai-task-hub 3.2.5

- Added "Agent Invocation Quickstart" section to documentation for easier integration and action payload examples.
- No changes to API endpoints or contracts; package behavior remains the same.
- Improved clarity on agent-side usage and invocation patterns in SKILL.md.

ai-task-hub 3.2.4

- Added gateway agent identifier and conversation_id format constraints to the Auth Contract.
- Host integration examples and guidance on authorization URL updated for clarity.
- Described agent binding bootstrap flow for `SYSTEM_NOT_FOUND` errors in detail.
- Minor clarifications for host integration and token issuance flows.

- Added section outlining host integration modes, including both "automatic" and "interactive fallback" approaches for task token handling.
- Clarified that the skill package itself does not open browser windows, persist credentials, or perform OAuth/token exchanges.
- No behavior changes to APIs or payloads. This update is documentation-focused and backwards compatible.

- Updated auth contract to require explicit token claims and action-specific scopes; clarified token lifetime policy and least-privilege scope usage.
- Documented required scope per action and introduced `account_read` scope for account balance/ledger requests.
- Added guidance for short-lived, action-scoped tokens to improve security and reduce unnecessary scopes.
- Minor documentation clarifications in SKILL.md and SKILL.zh-CN.md.

- Outbound API base URL is now locked to the default (`https://gateway-api.binaryworks.app`) for enhanced security; custom base URL overrides are no longer permitted in the published package.
- CLI argument order updated: legacy `base_url` parameter has been removed; all calls are pinned to the default API endpoint.
- Documentation updated in both English and Chinese to reflect the new base URL policy and usage changes.
- Internal scripts (`base-url.mjs`) and references (`openapi.json`, etc.) updated to match the base URL restriction and clarify public runtime contract.

**ai-task-hub 3.2.0 introduces account points balance and ledger lookup.**

- Added support for querying current points balance and recent points ledger (via `portal.account.balance` and `portal.account.ledger`).
- Updated documentation to detail new endpoints, common requests, and payload contracts.
- Extended search-friendly aliases to include points/ledger queries.
- Updated OpenAPI reference and code to orchestrate these new actions.

- Add guidance for host-side token bridge, clarifying that token issuance must happen outside the published package.
- Recommend host retry on AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED by refreshing and injecting a new AGENT_TASK_TOKEN.
- No changes to runtime, payload, or error contracts. 
- Documentation improvements in SKILL.md and SKILL.zh-CN.md for integration clarity.

ai-task-hub 3.1.4

- Renamed and refactored: skill is now "ai-task-hub" (formerly "skill-hub-gateway").
- Simplified focus: only orchestrates async AI task execution, polling, and visual presentation actions.
- Authentication is host-managed: requires and only accepts short-lived AGENT_TASK_TOKEN, no internal key exchange or payment logic.
- Portal and payment actions removed; recharge/payment flows now handled outside the skill.
- Local file uploads disabled; attachments must be pre-uploaded and provided as URLs.
- New unified script (`scripts/skill.mjs`) and internal helpers for agent-token orchestration.
- Documentation and contract updated to reflect new input/output/auth model.

- Refined authentication contract: Host must now auto-refresh and inject short-lived AGENT_TASK_TOKEN to reduce user-facing auth friction; removed support for issuing tokens via API key and UID.
- Updated environment requirements: Only AGENT_TASK_TOKEN is required; removed AGENT_API_KEY and AGENT_UID from requirements.
- Added new script: scripts/base-url.mjs.
- Updated documentation and examples in both English and Chinese guides.
- Updated references/openapi.json and related scripts for improved consistency.
